title: Infinite-mean initial-degree conjecture for the PARID model
statement: Let $r_k_{k\geq 1}$ be the distribution of the initial degrees in the PARID model, and suppose that it is a power-law distribution with exponent $\tau_{\scriptscriptstyle {\rm W}}\in(1,2)$. **PARID infinite-mean conjecture.** The degree sequence in the PARID model obeys a power law with the same exponent $\tau_{\scriptscriptstyle {\rm W}}$. Since $\tau_{\scriptscriptstyle {\rm W}}\in(1,2)$, the initial-degree distribution has infinite mean; the paper conjectures that its exponent determines the resulting degree sequence in this regime.
source_name: Maria Deijfen, Henri van den Esker, Remco van der Hofstad and Gerard Hooghiemstra, “A preferential attachment model with random initial degrees”, arXiv:0705.4151 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.4151

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2007).
